---
name: reference_owletto_sparkle_upgrade_verify
description: How to verify Owletto Mac in-app (Sparkle) upgrades work + the keys/identity involved
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: reference
  originSessionId: 786d2225-7d5d-4fae-a6cc-4dbf1a7f2e81
---

Owletto Mac auto-update = **Sparkle 2.9.1**, configured in `packages/owletto/apps/mac/Owletto/` (`OwlettoUpdater.swift` + `Info.plist`). Release pipeline = `.github/workflows/mac-release.yml`: signs each `Owletto.dmg` with `sign_update` (CI secret `SPARKLE_ED_PRIVATE_KEY`), attaches it to the `lobu-v<ver>` GitHub Release, and pushes a signed `<item>` into `appcast.xml` on the gh-pages branch. The workflow **fails the build** on bundle-id/name drift or missing `SUPublicEDKey` (guards the upgrade chain). Appcast generator: `scripts/sparkle/update-appcast.py`.

Stable facts:
- SUFeedURL: `https://lobu-ai.github.io/lobu/appcast.xml`
- SUPublicEDKey (ed25519, base64): `REDACTED`
- Signing identity: `Developer ID Application: Burak Emre Kabakci (CCV9Q352W3)`, hardened runtime, **notarized** (spctl: "Notarized Developer ID"). TeamID continuity (CCV9Q352W3) is what lets Sparkle apply updates silently.

Verify a release's upgrade WILL apply (2026-06-24, full chain validated for 12.1.0):
1. `curl -sL <SUFeedURL>` → newest item's `enclosure url`, `length`, `sparkle:edSignature`.
2. `curl -sIL <url>` → HTTP 200 + `content-length` == appcast `length`.
3. Download DMG, ed25519-verify the edSignature over the raw file bytes against SUPublicEDKey (Python `cryptography` Ed25519PublicKey). Valid sig ⇒ Sparkle accepts it ⇒ CI key matches bundled key.
4. `spctl -a -vvv -t install <app>` ⇒ "accepted / Notarized Developer ID".

Verify the updater STARTS / doesn't (deterministic behavioral A/B): Sparkle writes `SULastCheckTime` to the `com.owletto.mac` UserDefaults domain ONLY when a started updater performs a check. `defaults delete com.owletto.mac SULastCheckTime` to force a check due, launch, wait ~45s, re-read: written ⇒ updater ran; still unset ⇒ updater never started. Unified-log subsystem `org.sparkle-project.Sparkle` is SILENT at launch — don't rely on it. (Prior alert leaves a `NSWindow Frame SUUpdateAlert2` default key.)

Gotcha (FIXED+MERGED 2026-06-24, owletto#359 `9836010` / lobu#1549 `7f2cf9c30`): local **Debug** builds are stamped `MARKETING_VERSION=0.1.0` (CI overrides per-tag via `xcodebuild "MARKETING_VERSION=<tag>"`; pbxproj value is a never-shipped placeholder, but Info.plist uses `$(MARKETING_VERSION)` so it can't be deleted), so a started Sparkle updater always saw the release as newer and nagged "Update to vX.Y.Z" (+ would silently auto-update, `SUAutomaticallyUpdate=true`). Fix = `startingUpdater: false` in `#if DEBUG` in `OwlettoUpdater.swift` — do NOT flip the persisted `automaticallyChecksForUpdates` pref (leaks into the Release app via the shared domain). Judge real upgrades from a properly-installed `/Applications/Owletto.app`, not a DerivedData debug build (`Apple Development`-signed, Xcode clobbers on next build). Related: [[project_owletto_menubar_cloud_switch]], [[reference_owletto_local_context_8787]].

name: project_device_behavior_exit_report_delivery
description: "Device Behavior exit reports are replayable via finalize_attempt; #2361 MERGED a23ad740f; ROLLED OUT prod 9f0c3e161; behavioural verify BLOCKED on a Mac release"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: 259b2997-9a73-4761-987d-67f0a02cf9fe
  modified: 2026-07-30T19:49:23.510Z
---

**#2361 MERGED `a23ad740f` 2026-07-30.** Device `complete-behavior` now: window Behavior with
budget left → `status: resume` (run stays claimed, Mac re-spawns); budget spent → fail with
`reason_code: missing_complete_window`; event turn → completes with no window.

**The delivery contract (this is the load-bearing part).** Exit reports carry `finalize_attempt`
= the `finalize_nudge_count` the reporting spawn ran under. When the stored count is already past
it, the report was answered with a resume the device never saw, so the server **re-serves the same
grant and consumes nothing**. Without it, replaying a report whose response was lost read the
already-bumped count, found the budget spent, and failed the run one spawn early — a lost response
reinterpreted as work that happened. Mac half (owletto#654) splits execution from delivery:
executor failures stay terminal; a failed POST re-sends the identical report, and when the outcome
stays unknown it reports **nothing** and leaves the run claimed for the heartbeat-stale reaper.
Never convert an ambiguous delivery outcome into `completeWithError`. See
[[feedback_gateway_predicate_cannot_replace_worker_state]].

**Turn runs must not be told to call completeWindow** (owletto#656). The device prompt was
unconditional, so an event turn minted a canvas and completed through the window path, making the
server's no-window branch unreachable. `trigger_execution` already reaches the device nested in
`payload.event.payload` (poll ships `approved_input` verbatim) — no server change needed to branch
on it.

**Nudge text took `watcher_id`; the SDK only accepts `behavior_id`** (`sandbox/namespaces/knowledge.ts:43`).
A resumed run was handed instructions that could not work. Caught by `make review-fix`, not by review.

**Every exit-report transition is predicated on `claimed_by = worker_id`.** Proven load-bearing:
`authorizeRunForWorker` did NOT reject a wrong-worker report on this path in the integration
harness, so the SQL predicates are the real gate.

**Prod rollout CONFIRMED 2026-07-30 ~20:15.** Both `summaries-prod` api pods on
`lobu-app:20260730-190004-001760`, deployed SHA `9f0c3e161`, and
`git merge-base --is-ancestor a23ad740f 9f0c3e161` passes. The server half is live.

**Behavioural prod-verify BLOCKED on a Mac release, not owed to laziness.** The device half
(resume re-spawn, turn prompt) needs a Mac build carrying owletto#654/#656, and the newest
`mac-release.yml` run is v14.7.1 from lobu `a6aab9367` (2026-07-29) — it predates both. The
paired Mac mini `mac-e74661e8-…` heartbeats every ~6s but runs the old binary, so dispatching to
it would exercise the OLD device code and prove nothing. No device run has touched the new server
paths either: newest `claimed_by LIKE 'mac-%'` run is 808754 at 17:20Z, before the 19:59 build.
**Unblock — a release is NOT enough.** `mac-release.yml` does fire on `release: published` (not
dispatch-only), so the next `lobu-v*` release builds the DMG automatically. But **the paired Macs
will not consume it.** Both report `app_version 0.1.0`, which is the Xcode project's default
`MARKETING_VERSION` (`CFBundleShortVersionString = $(MARKETING_VERSION)`, CI overrides it per
release tag) — so they run **locally built binaries, not releases**. `OwlettoUpdater.swift` does
not even start the scheduled Sparkle updater for such builds: 0.1.0 always looks behind the
appcast and an update "can't install cleanly over a DerivedData dev build". **The Mac mini must be
rebuilt from owletto main on that machine**, or have a release DMG installed over it.
Vintage lower bound: it advertises `connector_manifests`, which landed 2026-07-05, so the build is
from on/after that date — not datable more precisely from off-machine.
(Contrast: `/Applications/Owletto.app` on the MacBook Pro reports `12.1.0`, a genuine release from
2026-06-20 — that is what an installed release looks like.) Simulating a device worker against prod instead needs a minted worker credential —
no prod PAT exists locally.

Prod DB access for this check: `kubectl exec -n summaries-prod lobu-ai-prod-db-1 -c postgres --
psql -U postgres -d owletto`. The database is **`owletto`**, not `app` (`app` holds 1 table);
device rows are in `device_workers` (`last_seen_at`, no `status` column), not `workers`.

Related: [[project_deployment_recycle_redesign]], [[reference_squash_merge_breaks_ancestry_checks]].

summary, `signature: feeds.trigger(input: { feed_id: number; dry_run?: boolean })`,
and the example. `client.feeds.trigger({feed_id, dry_run:true})` forwarded the
flag (visible in `sdk_call_trace.args`) and the result echoed `dry_run: true` —
the echo only fires when the flag was HONOURED, so it is not a silent drop.

persisted **zero** events — newest midas event stayed 2026-07-18, ~2 weeks old.
`dry_run: true` is stored on the runs row and readable via `feeds.get`
`recent_runs`. (Run ended `failed`; midas was already failing — 3 prior
failed/timeout runs — so that is pre-existing, not caused by the dry run.)

`describeSyncRunSkip` path (second immediate trigger → "Sync already pending or
running for this feed"). The four NEW messages are **not reachable in prod
without creating test data**: every active feed has its org-scoped
connector_definition (`org_def = 1` for all 33), and there is no *collected*
postgres feed (452 is virtual → rejected earlier with "Feed is virtual"). Those
branches remain CI-covered only.

prod — no Mac has shipped that build via Sparkle. Useful negative: the existing

build ships: all 10 manifests must install.

**#2395 PROBE ANSWERED THE OPEN QUESTION.** From the
`exec-sandbox-backend-probe` job on main (run 30610832069):

    - systemd-run --user: **works** (viable alternative backend)
    kernel.unprivileged_userns_clone=unset
    kernel.apparmor_restrict_unprivileged_userns=unset

**`systemd-run --user` is viable on Blacksmith runners.** Caveat that matters: a
GitHub runner is NOT the managed k8s pod where bwrap's uid_map is restricted, so
this does not establish it works in the cluster — it is the first data point,
not the conclusion. `bwrap: not installed` is expected here (this job has no
install step, unlike the exec-sandbox test jobs).

No test data left behind: the dry run wrote nothing and ended terminal, so the

**Shell access is not available, and 14.8.0 wouldn't give it either.**

**Status: root cause FIXED 2026-07-30 (branch `feat/menubar-perms`). Remote swap of
`/Applications/Owletto.app` was performed 4x that night on the Mac mini over SSH with zero
downtime.** Keep this file for the mechanism, not the prohibition.

**The original failure (2026-07-30, ~19:55 UTC).** Replacing the bundle took the mini's worker
offline and could NOT be restored remotely — restoring the byte-identical backup hung the OLD build
in the same frame, because TCC keys its record to bundle path + code identity and a different binary
there invalidates the entry for both. `pkill UserNotificationCenter`, killing the per-user `tccd`,
and `tccutil reset SystemPolicyAppData com.owletto.mac` all failed. Recovery needed a human at the
screen.

**Why it bricked — the real bug.** `AppState` is `@MainActor`. `currentCapabilities` is a *computed
property* that called `WhatsAppLocalSyncService.isAvailable()`, a blocking
`FileHandle(forReadingAtPath:)` on the WhatsApp group container. A new binary makes TCC re-evaluate,
so that `open()` blocks until a human answers a dialog — parking the menu bar, poll loop, heartbeat
and every other connector. `sample <pid>` showing 100% of samples in `__open` under that stack is the
fingerprint. **The language was never the problem; the placement was.** Same call from a background
thread is harmless.

**Fixes applied (all in `AppState.swift`):**
1. `whatsAppArchiveReadable` — cached flag, probed via `Task.detached`, read by
   `currentCapabilities`. Main actor never does I/O.
2. **Probe once per launch**, forced only on explicit grant / toggle. Critical: poll interval is
   `actionPollInterval = 10`s whenever computer use is active, so probing in `syncNow()` meant a TCC
   dialog **every 10 seconds** — the user answered and it reappeared. This was a real reported
   symptom, not theoretical.
3. `refreshFDAStatus()` had the identical bug (blocking `open` of `knowledgeC.db` on the main actor,
   every poll). Now detached + 60s throttle — it re-polls because FDA genuinely changes at runtime.
4. Operand order: `isAvailable() && !whatsAppDisabled` ran the probe BEFORE the kill switch, so the
   user-facing toggle could not prevent the hang. Flag now short-circuits first. Same fix applied to
   the `system_audio` check.

**Not a bug, checked:** `hasHealthKit` = `HealthKitSyncService.hasBeenRequested`, a UserDefaults
flag rather than a live query. Apple deliberately does not expose HealthKit *read* authorization
(it would leak health data by inference), so a stored flag is the standard workaround.

**Safe remote-swap recipe (verified 4x):** `ditto -c -k --sequesterRsrc --keepParent` → `scp` →
`ditto -x -k` on the target → `codesign -v --deep --strict` → back up the old bundle → quit → `ditto`
into `/Applications` → `open -a`. Then verify: `sample <pid>` main thread parked in
`_BlockUntilNextEventMatchingListInMode` (idle, healthy) and the `device_workers` row heartbeating.
Expect capabilities gated on TCC to drop until the user answers the prompt — the app stays alive and
they return on the next forced probe. That degradation is the fix working.

**Diagnosing without installing:** grep the binary — `strings Owletto | grep -F "<known literal>"`.
Absence is weak evidence (not all Swift literals land in `strings`); `cmp` against your own build is
decisive.

**Seeing the screen:** the computer-use MCP CANNOT drive Owletto (`LSUIElement` app →
`request_access` returns `not_installed`; see [[feedback_computer_use_cant_grant_owletto]]). But
plain `screencapture -x` via Bash works fine on the local Mac. Over SSH to the mini it fails with
"could not create image from display" — no window-server session.

**Opening the menu bar popover yourself (no human needed).** computer-use can't reach an
`LSUIElement` app, but AppleScript UI scripting can, because System Events carries its OWN
Accessibility grant — Owletto's missing grants are irrelevant:

```bash
osascript -e 'tell application "System Events" to tell process "Owletto" \
  to click menu bar item 1 of menu bar 2'
screencapture -x /tmp/popover.png    # then crop/zoom to read the chips
osascript -e 'tell application "System Events" to key code 53'   # Escape to close
```

`menu bar 2` is the status bar (`menu bar 1` is the system one). This closes the self-verification
loop: you can confirm a menu-bar UI change landed without asking the user to look. Verified
2026-07-30 — read the permission chips and confirmed a removed section was gone.

Merged 2026-07-31. Prod-verify owed (see wakeup gate).

**One unknown manifest key drops EVERY connector on that device.** In
`device-manifests.ts`, an unrecognised key throws → `accepted = false` for the
whole payload → `poll.ts:271` declines to replace the device inventory (correct:
a malformed poll must not look like removal) → `{}` is written. Measured on the
10 real Mac manifests: without the fix `INSTALLED: (NONE)`; with it, all 10
including `apple.computer_use`. So owletto#669's new `os.shell` would have taken
down screen time, calendar, photos and WhatsApp too.

Cause: `connectorKeyAllowedForPlatform` (a per-connector opt-in / review
checkpoint) drifted from `OS_CAPABILITIES` in `@lobu/core`, which already
allowlisted `os.shell`. Shipped as an **exact-match** `key === 'os.shell'`
(Codesmith bot's version), not my `os.` prefix — the prefix would have
pre-authorized `os.files`/`os.notifications` on a shell-exec surface and removed
the checkpoint. `os.shell` runs arbitrary commands via `zsh -l -c`; user
explicitly approved enabling it.

**Slug race (#2399).** `ensureDeviceConnectorWired` derives the connection slug
from the manifest DISPLAY NAME, `connections_org_slug_unique` is per-ORG, but
the advisory lock is keyed `(userId, connectorKey)`. **Lock scope ≠ uniqueness
scope**, so two different keys take different locks and race. A source comment
claimed this "can't be raced" — it was wrong and is now corrected. Fixed with a
bounded single retry outside the tx (an aborted tx cannot be continued).
Symptom was a ~1-in-8 flake in `device-connector-manifests.test.ts`.

Correction worth keeping: the error was **never invisible** —
`ensureDeviceConnectorWired` already caught and logged it at error level, so
"allSettled swallows it" was wrong. A logging-only fix was written, found to be
dead code, reverted.

**Is feature X actually IN the shipped Mac release?** Do NOT reason from "the release is newer
than the PR" — the Mac app lives in the `packages/owletto` submodule, so what shipped is the
submodule PIN at the release's lobu SHA, which can lag main by hours. Recipe (used 2026-07-31 to
show v14.8.0 lacks `os.shell` despite being released after owletto#669):

```bash
gh run list --workflow mac-release.yml -L 1 --json displayTitle,headSha   # → lobu SHA for the tag
PIN=$(git ls-tree <lobuSHA> packages/owletto | awk '{print $3}')          # owletto SHA that BUILT it
cd packages/owletto && git fetch -q origin
gh pr view <n> --repo lobu-ai/owletto --json mergeCommit --jq .mergeCommit.oid
git merge-base --is-ancestor <prMergeSHA> "$PIN"                          # exit 0 ⇒ shipped
git ls-tree "$PIN" apps/mac/Owletto/ConnectorManifests/                   # what manifests shipped
git log --oneline "$PIN"..origin/main                                     # what did NOT ship
```

Note `git grep <pat> origin/main` in the PARENT repo does not descend into the submodule — it
silently returns nothing. Grep from inside `packages/owletto` against ITS `origin/main`.

Also: `curl` of the appcast hits a GitHub Pages CDN cache and can serve a stale newest-item for a
while after the gh-pages commit lands. Append a cache-buster (`?cb=$(date +%s)`) before concluding
a version is missing — measured 2026-07-31, plain curl showed 14.7.1 while 14.8.0 was live.

content.text:
Yes — SSH to `mini` works over Tailscale. But probing it turned up something that changes the recommendation, including a correction to what I told you earlier.

**Sparkle is not dormant on the mini — it's stuck at the apply step.**

```
Owletto            started Fri 31 Jul 02:09   (up 16h, never quits)
Sparkle Autoupdate started Fri 31 Jul 16:17   (parked 2h)
SULastCheckTime  = 2026-07-31 15:17:40 +0000
```

It downloaded and staged **14.8.0** — notarized, `Developer ID Application: Burak Emre Kabakci (CCV9Q352W3)`, spctl `accepted`. The installer is waiting for the host app to terminate, and a menubar `LSUIElement` app on an unattended mini never quits. There's also a stale **14.5.0** staged from 28 Jul that never applied — so this has been silently failing for at least three days, not once.

So my earlier claim that Sparkle wouldn't update this build was wrong: it checks and downloads fine. The failure is at the swap, not the check.

**Direct confirmation that 14.8.0 lacks os.shell** — from the actual staged bundle, not inference: `ConnectorManifests/` has 9 files, no `os_shell.json`, and `strings Owletto | grep -c "os.shell"` = 0.

**No Xcode on the mini** (Command Line Tools only), so a manual build has to happen here on the MacBook (Xcode 26.2) and ship over via the ditto/scp recipe.

That gives two real options, and they differ in a way that matters:

| | Restart Owletto on the mini | Build here + swap |
|---|---|---|
| Applies | staged **14.8.0**, notarized Developer ID | owletto main, **Apple Development**-signed |
| os.shell | no | **yes**, today |
| Signing identity | moves off local build onto release lineage | stays a local build — perpetuates this exact problem |
| Effort | one `killall`/relaunch | full build + transfer |

Current `/Applications/Owletto.app` is signed `Apple Development: … (8NVN2W85G3)`; the staged one is `Developer ID`. Same TeamIdentifier, but the cert type change is a code-identity change, so **TCC will re-evaluate and permission-gated capabilities will drop until someone answers the prompts on that machine.** That's true for either option, and it's why I'm asking rather than just doing it — if nobody's near the mini, its connectors sit degraded.

My recommendation: restart Owletto to take the staged 14.8.0 (fixes the signing-identity mess and gets you the #654/#656 device half), then cut 14.9.0 off lobu main for os.shell and let Sparkle carry it — assuming we also fix the never-quits-so-never-updates condition, which is a genuine bug worth its own issue.

Want me to trigger the restart? And should I open an issue for the stuck-installer condition — an app that stages updates forever and never applies them is going to keep doing this on every unattended Mac.

name: mac-release

# Builds and ships Owletto for Mac, then attaches Owletto.dmg to the existing
# `lobu-v<version>` GitHub Release (so releases/latest/download/Owletto.dmg always
# resolves) and signs an entry into the Sparkle appcast so installed apps can
# auto-update.
#
# The Mac source lives in the private `lobu-ai/owletto` repo, mounted here as
# the `packages/owletto` submodule. Releases ship from this (public) repo so the
# DMG download URL and Sparkle appcast URL stay reachable to anonymous users —
# private-repo Releases would 404 without auth.
#
# Two modes, picked automatically from whether the Developer ID cert secret is
# set — adding the secrets is the *only* thing needed to flip from stopgap to
# production; nothing in this file changes:
#
#   • SIGNED (production)  — APPLE_CERT_P12_BASE64 present: Developer ID
#       codesign + hardened runtime + notarize + staple. DMG opens with no
#       Gatekeeper warning.
#   • UNSIGNED (stopgap)   — that secret empty: ad-hoc-signed app, no
#       notarization. Works, but the first launch needs right-click → Open
#       ("unidentified developer"). This is what runs until the Apple Developer
#       Program membership + Developer ID cert exist.
#
# ── To switch to SIGNED: add these repo secrets, that's it ──────────────────
#   APPLE_CERT_P12_BASE64            base64 of a "Developer ID Application" .p12
#   APPLE_CERT_PASSWORD              password for that .p12
#   APPLE_TEAM_ID                    10-char Apple Developer team id
#   APPLE_ID                         Apple ID email used for notarization
#   APPLE_APP_PASSWORD               app-specific password for that Apple ID
#
#
# ── Optional: when shipping a restricted entitlement (e.g. HealthKit) ───────
#   APPLE_PROVISION_PROFILE_BASE64   base64 of a Developer ID .provisionprofile
#                                    issued for com.owletto.mac, carrying the
#                                    restricted capability
#   APPLE_PROVISION_PROFILE_NAME     the profile's exact name as shown in the
#                                    Apple Developer portal (Profiles list).
#                                    Passed to xcodebuild as
#                                    PROVISIONING_PROFILE_SPECIFIER.
#
# Current Owletto.entitlements carries no restricted entitlements, so the
# provisioning-profile secrets are optional. To add HealthKit (or another
# restricted entitlement) later:
#   1. Submit a Capability Request to Apple
#      (https://developer.apple.com/contact/request/capability-request/) —
#      the App ID checkbox alone isn't enough; the profile won't carry the
#      entitlement until Apple approves.
#   2. Re-issue the Developer ID profile (it gets the entitlement only after
#      approval is on file).
#   3. Set APPLE_PROVISION_PROFILE_BASE64 + APPLE_PROVISION_PROFILE_NAME.
# The "Install provisioning profile" step is skipped automatically when
# APPLE_PROVISION_PROFILE_BASE64 is empty.
#
# Sparkle auto-updates: `SPARKLE_ED_PRIVATE_KEY` (64-byte base64 of seed||pub)
# is required. The job signs Owletto.dmg with `sign_update` and pushes a new
# <item> into appcast.xml on the gh-pages branch (served at
# https://lobu-ai.github.io/lobu/appcast.xml — that URL is in Info.plist as
# SUFeedURL). Public key is in Info.plist:SUPublicEDKey.

on:
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      version:
        description: 'Release version, e.g. 0.42.0 (must have a lobu-v<version> release)'
        required: true
  # Auto-fires every time release-please publishes a GitHub Release (which
  # happens once a `chore(main): release lobu X.Y.Z` PR is merged). The job
  # guard below filters out anything that isn't a `lobu-v*` tag, so other
  # release-creating workflows in this repo don't accidentally rebuild the
  # Mac DMG.
  release:
    types: [published]

permissions:
  contents: write

jobs:
  release:
    runs-on: blacksmith-6vcpu-macos-15
    if: >-
      github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch'
      || startsWith(github.event.release.tag_name, 'lobu-v')
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7

      # Mac source lives in the owletto submodule; need the deploy key to clone.
      - id: submodule
        uses: ./.github/actions/setup-submodule
        with:
          deploy-key: ${{ secrets.OWLETTO_WEB_DEPLOY_KEY }}

      # Release contract — fail fast rather than build a wrong/missing artifact:
      #   1. The deploy key must work. The setup-submodule action writes a stub
      #      package.json when the key is absent; that's fine for CI on forks but
      #      catastrophic for a release (we'd ship an empty DMG or fail late on
      #      a missing project). Make it fatal here.
      #   2. The submodule must point at lobu-ai/owletto. If the URL drifted we
      #      could be releasing the wrong codebase entirely.
      #   3. The Mac Xcode project + bundle paths the rest of this workflow
      #      assumes must actually exist at the pinned SHA. Otherwise the
      #      `lobster-mark.svg` → `owletto-mark.svg` style of silent rename on
      #      the owletto side would only surface inside `xcodebuild`.
      #   4-7. The scheme name, app display name, bundle identifier, and
      #      Sparkle public key must match what the rest of the workflow and
      #      installed apps depend on. A rename inside owletto (e.g. scheme
      #      target renames, bundle id `com.owletto.mac` drift)
      #      would pass the path checks above but break the build or, worse,
      #      silently break auto-update for installed users.
      - name: Verify release contract (submodule + Mac source layout)
        shell: bash
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          if [ "${{ steps.submodule.outputs.stubbed }}" = "true" ]; then
            echo "::error::Submodule was stubbed — OWLETTO_WEB_DEPLOY_KEY is missing or invalid. Aborting release."
            exit 1
          fi
          remote_url=$(git -C packages/owletto config --get remote.origin.url)
          case "$remote_url" in
            *lobu-ai/owletto.git|*lobu-ai/owletto) ;;
            *)
              echo "::error::packages/owletto origin is '$remote_url' — expected lobu-ai/owletto. Aborting release."
              exit 1
              ;;
          esac
          for required in \
            packages/owletto/apps/mac/Owletto.xcodeproj \
            packages/owletto/apps/mac/Owletto/Info.plist \
            scripts/sparkle/update-appcast.py
          do
            if [ ! -e "$required" ]; then
              echo "::error::Required release path missing: $required"
              exit 1
            fi
          done

          # 4. The Xcode scheme must still be named 'Owletto'. The rest of
          #    this workflow passes `-scheme Owletto` to xcodebuild; if a rename
          #    happens upstream, the path checks above still pass and we'd only
          #    find out late inside xcodebuild.
          #
          #    Scope the check to the schemes list via `-list -json`. The plain
          #    `-list` text output has both `Targets:` and `Schemes:` sections,
          #    so a `grep '^  Owletto$'` could match a target named 'Owletto'
          #    even after the scheme was renamed.
          SCHEMES=$(xcodebuild -project packages/owletto/apps/mac/Owletto.xcodeproj -list -json 2>/dev/null \
            | python3 -c "import json,sys; print('\n'.join(json.load(sys.stdin)['project']['schemes']))")
          if ! echo "$SCHEMES" | grep -qE '^Owletto$'; then
            echo "::error::Expected scheme 'Owletto' missing from project schemes (got: $SCHEMES)"
            exit 1
          fi

          # 5. CFBundleName + CFBundleDisplayName must stay 'Owletto'. These
          #    are what users see in Finder / the menu bar / "About"; a silent
          #    rename here would ship a DMG that installs as a different app
          #    next to existing installs.
          EXPECTED_BUNDLE_NAME="Owletto"
          for key in CFBundleName CFBundleDisplayName; do
            actual=$(/usr/libexec/PlistBuddy -c "Print :$key" \
              packages/owletto/apps/mac/Owletto/Info.plist 2>/dev/null || true)
            if [ "$actual" != "$EXPECTED_BUNDLE_NAME" ]; then
              echo "::error::Info.plist:$key is '$actual', expected '$EXPECTED_BUNDLE_NAME'"
              exit 1
            fi
          done

          # 6. PRODUCT_BUNDLE_IDENTIFIER in project.pbxproj must stay
          #    com.owletto.mac across ALL build configurations. CFBundleIdentifier
          #    in Info.plist resolves to $(PRODUCT_BUNDLE_IDENTIFIER) at build
          #    time, so the real value lives in the pbxproj build settings.
          #    The URL scheme, Keychain service name, and Sparkle update path
          #    are all keyed off this — a change here breaks the upgrade
          #    contract for installed apps.
          #
          #    Assert the set of distinct values is exactly {com.owletto.mac},
          #    not "some occurrence equals com.owletto.mac". A simple grep
          #    would still pass if one config drifted while another stale
          #    occurrence stayed correct.
          EXPECTED_BUNDLE_ID="com.owletto.mac"
          distinct_ids=$(grep -E 'PRODUCT_BUNDLE_IDENTIFIER = ' \
            packages/owletto/apps/mac/Owletto.xcodeproj/project.pbxproj \
            | sed -E 's/.*PRODUCT_BUNDLE_IDENTIFIER = ([^;]+);.*/\1/' \
            | sort -u)
          if [ "$distinct_ids" != "$EXPECTED_BUNDLE_ID" ]; then
            echo "::error::PRODUCT_BUNDLE_IDENTIFIER must be exactly '${EXPECTED_BUNDLE_ID}' across all configs (got: $distinct_ids). Bundle id drift breaks installed-app upgrades."
            exit 1
          fi

          # 7. Sparkle public key must still be in Info.plist. Installed apps
          #    verify update signatures against SUPublicEDKey; if the key is
          #    removed or rotated server-side without matching a key the
          #    installed app trusts, auto-update breaks silently.
          #
          #    Use PlistBuddy so the check matches an actual plist key, not
          #    text inside an XML comment.
          if ! /usr/libexec/PlistBuddy -c "Print :SUPublicEDKey" \
            packages/owletto/apps/mac/Owletto/Info.plist >/dev/null 2>&1; then
            echo "::error::SUPublicEDKey missing from Info.plist — installed apps cannot verify updates"
            exit 1
          fi

fi

      # workflow_dispatch carries the version as an input; release-triggered
      # runs carry it on github.event.release.tag_name in the form
      # `lobu-v<X.Y.Z>` (set by release-please). Strip the prefix so the
      # value matches the dispatch input shape.
      #
      # Untrusted inputs are passed through `env:` (never interpolated
      # straight into a `run:` block) and validated against a strict semver
      # regex before they reach $GITHUB_OUTPUT — a tag like
      # `lobu-v7.2.0;rm -rf /` would pass the prefix-only job guard but is
      # rejected here, so downstream steps that interpolate `steps.v.outputs.version`
      # (notarytool, the release-attach action, the appcast publisher) can't
      # be tricked into executing shell.
      - name: Resolve version
        id: v
        env:
          EVENT_NAME: ${{ github.event_name }}
          DISPATCH_VERSION: ${{ github.event.inputs.version }}
          RELEASE_TAG: ${{ github.event.release.tag_name }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          if [ "$EVENT_NAME" = "workflow_dispatch" ]; then
            VERSION="$DISPATCH_VERSION"
          else
            VERSION="${RELEASE_TAG#lobu-v}"
          fi
          if [ -z "$VERSION" ]; then
            echo "::error::Could not resolve a version (event=$EVENT_NAME)"
            exit 1
          fi
          # Strict semver-ish: digits.digits.digits with an optional `-prerelease`
          # suffix of alphanum / dot / hyphen. Anything else (shell metachars,
          # path traversal, whitespace) is rejected.
          if ! printf '%s' "$VERSION" | grep -Eq '^[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+(-[0-9A-Za-z.-]+)?$'; then
            echo "::error::Refusing to use version '$VERSION' — not a valid semver."
            exit 1
          fi
          echo "version=$VERSION" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

      - name: Detect signing mode
        id: mode
        env:
          CERT_P12_BASE64: ${{ secrets.APPLE_CERT_P12_BASE64 }}
        run: |
          if [ -n "$CERT_P12_BASE64" ]; then
            echo "signed=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "::notice::Building a SIGNED + notarized DMG."
          else
            echo "signed=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "::warning::APPLE_CERT_P12_BASE64 not set — building an UNSIGNED DMG (Gatekeeper warns on first open). Add the signing secrets to get a notarized build."
          fi

      # ── SIGNED path: import the Developer ID cert into an ephemeral keychain ──
      - name: Import signing certificate
        if: steps.mode.outputs.signed == 'true'
        env:
          CERT_P12_BASE64: ${{ secrets.APPLE_CERT_P12_BASE64 }}
          CERT_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.APPLE_CERT_PASSWORD }}
        run: |
          KEYCHAIN="$RUNNER_TEMP/build.keychain-db"
          KEYCHAIN_PASSWORD="$(openssl rand -base64 24)"
          security create-keychain -p "$KEYCHAIN_PASSWORD" "$KEYCHAIN"
          security set-keychain-settings -lut 21600 "$KEYCHAIN"
          security unlock-keychain -p "$KEYCHAIN_PASSWORD" "$KEYCHAIN"
          echo "$CERT_P12_BASE64" | base64 --decode > "$RUNNER_TEMP/cert.p12"
          security import "$RUNNER_TEMP/cert.p12" -k "$KEYCHAIN" -P "$CERT_PASSWORD" -T /usr/bin/codesign
          security set-key-partition-list -S apple-tool:,apple: -s -k "$KEYCHAIN_PASSWORD" "$KEYCHAIN"
          security list-keychains -d user -s "$KEYCHAIN"
          security default-keychain -s "$KEYCHAIN"

      # Install the Developer ID provisioning profile so Xcode embeds it
      # during the archive step. Only needed when Owletto.entitlements
      # carries a restricted entitlement (HealthKit, Family Controls, etc.)
      # — otherwise notarization rejects the build with "App is using a
      # restricted entitlement without a matching provisioning profile."
      # Skipped silently when APPLE_PROVISION_PROFILE_BASE64 isn't set, so
      # builds with only standard entitlements just work.
      #
      # Xcode looks in ~/Library/MobileDevice/Provisioning Profiles. The
      # filename should match the profile's UUID; we extract it from the
      # decoded plist so the same secret keeps working across re-issues.
      - name: Install provisioning profile
        id: profile
        if: steps.mode.outputs.signed == 'true' && env.PROFILE_BASE64 != ''
        env:
          PROFILE_BASE64: ${{ secrets.APPLE_PROVISION_PROFILE_BASE64 }}
          PROFILE_NAME: ${{ secrets.APPLE_PROVISION_PROFILE_NAME }}
        run: |
          if [ -z "$PROFILE_NAME" ]; then
            echo "::error::APPLE_PROVISION_PROFILE_BASE64 is set but APPLE_PROVISION_PROFILE_NAME is missing."
            exit 1
          fi
          DEST_DIR="$HOME/Library/MobileDevice/Provisioning Profiles"
          mkdir -p "$DEST_DIR"
          TMP_PROFILE="$RUNNER_TEMP/profile.provisionprofile"
          echo "$PROFILE_BASE64" | base64 --decode > "$TMP_PROFILE"
          # Extract UUID from the CMS-wrapped plist inside the .provisionprofile.
          security cms -D -i "$TMP_PROFILE" > "$RUNNER_TEMP/profile.plist"
          UUID=$(/usr/libexec/PlistBuddy -c "Print :UUID" "$RUNNER_TEMP/profile.plist")
          if [ -z "$UUID" ]; then
            echo "::error::Could not extract UUID from provisioning profile."
            exit 1
          fi
          cp "$TMP_PROFILE" "$DEST_DIR/$UUID.provisionprofile"
          echo "installed=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "::notice::Installed provisioning profile '$PROFILE_NAME' ($UUID)"

      # PROVISIONING_PROFILE_SPECIFIER is only passed when a profile was
      # installed in the previous step. Without it, xcodebuild defaults to
      # no embedded profile, which is correct for builds using only standard
      # entitlements. Use a bash array so profile names with spaces
      # (e.g. "Owletto Developer ID") survive word-splitting.
      #
      # SPM-vendored Sparkle ships nested helpers (Updater.app, Autoupdate,
      # Downloader.xpc, Installer.xpc) that Xcode's archive does NOT sign
      # with Developer ID / secure timestamp — Apple's notary then rejects
      # the bundle with "binary not signed with valid Developer ID" /
      # "signature does not include a secure timestamp" errors. The "Re-sign
      # Sparkle helpers" step after archive re-signs each helper leaf-first
      # with --options runtime + --timestamp, then re-signs the umbrella
      # Owletto.app so the new helper signatures are sealed into the parent.
      - name: Archive (signed)
        if: steps.mode.outputs.signed == 'true'
        env:
          PROFILE_NAME: ${{ secrets.APPLE_PROVISION_PROFILE_NAME }}
        run: |
          ARGS=(
            -project packages/owletto/apps/mac/Owletto.xcodeproj
            -scheme Owletto
            -configuration Release
            -archivePath "$RUNNER_TEMP/Owletto.xcarchive"
            archive
            CODE_SIGN_STYLE=Manual
            "CODE_SIGN_IDENTITY=Developer ID Application"
            "DEVELOPMENT_TEAM=${{ secrets.APPLE_TEAM_ID }}"
            ENABLE_HARDENED_RUNTIME=YES
            "MARKETING_VERSION=${{ steps.v.outputs.version }}"
          )
          if [ "${{ steps.profile.outputs.installed }}" = "true" ]; then
            ARGS+=("PROVISIONING_PROFILE_SPECIFIER=$PROFILE_NAME")

      # via SPM, and notarytool rejects the bundle on that basis. Sign
      # leaf-first (innermost binaries → enclosing bundles → framework →
      # umbrella app) so each enclosing seal includes the new inner
      # signatures. --options runtime is required because the parent app
      # uses Hardened Runtime; --timestamp is required for notarization.
      - name: Re-sign Sparkle helpers
        if: steps.mode.outputs.signed == 'true'
        run: |
          set -e
          APP="$RUNNER_TEMP/Owletto.xcarchive/Products/Applications/Owletto.app"
          SPARKLE="$APP/Contents/Frameworks/Sparkle.framework/Versions/B"
          OPTS=(--force --options runtime --timestamp --sign "Developer ID Application")

          # XPC services (each has an inner Mach-O + an outer bundle).
          if [ -d "$SPARKLE/XPCServices/Downloader.xpc" ]; then
            codesign "${OPTS[@]}" "$SPARKLE/XPCServices/Downloader.xpc/Contents/MacOS/Downloader"
            codesign "${OPTS[@]}" "$SPARKLE/XPCServices/Downloader.xpc"
          fi
          if [ -d "$SPARKLE/XPCServices/Installer.xpc" ]; then
            codesign "${OPTS[@]}" "$SPARKLE/XPCServices/Installer.xpc/Contents/MacOS/Installer"
            codesign "${OPTS[@]}" "$SPARKLE/XPCServices/Installer.xpc"
          fi

          # Updater.app and standalone Autoupdate Mach-O.
          if [ -d "$SPARKLE/Updater.app" ]; then
            codesign "${OPTS[@]}" "$SPARKLE/Updater.app/Contents/MacOS/Updater"
            codesign "${OPTS[@]}" "$SPARKLE/Updater.app"
          fi
          if [ -f "$SPARKLE/Autoupdate" ]; then
            codesign "${OPTS[@]}" "$SPARKLE/Autoupdate"
          fi

          # Framework itself + umbrella app last, so they seal the
          # updated inner signatures.
          codesign "${OPTS[@]}" "$APP/Contents/Frameworks/Sparkle.framework"
          codesign "${OPTS[@]}" "$APP"

          # Verify before we hand it to notarytool.
          codesign --verify --deep --strict --verbose=2 "$APP"

      - name: Archive (unsigned, ad-hoc)
        if: steps.mode.outputs.signed != 'true'
        run: |
          xcodebuild \
            -project packages/owletto/apps/mac/Owletto.xcodeproj -scheme Owletto -configuration Release \
            -archivePath "$RUNNER_TEMP/Owletto.xcarchive" archive \
            CODE_SIGNING_ALLOWED=NO \
            MARKETING_VERSION="${{ steps.v.outputs.version }}"
          # arm64 apps must carry at least an ad-hoc signature to launch at all;
          # this also lets users do right-click → Open past "unidentified
          # developer". A real Developer ID + notarization removes that prompt.
          codesign --force --deep --sign - "$RUNNER_TEMP/Owletto.xcarchive/Products/Applications/Owletto.app"

      - name: Build DMG
        run: |
          APP="$RUNNER_TEMP/Owletto.xcarchive/Products/Applications/Owletto.app"
          test -d "$APP" || { echo "::error::Owletto.app missing from archive"; exit 1; }
          STAGE="$RUNNER_TEMP/dmg-stage"; mkdir -p "$STAGE"; cp -R "$APP" "$STAGE/"
          brew install create-dmg
          # create-dmg can exit non-zero on cosmetic AppleScript hiccups while
          # still producing the image, so verify the artifact instead of $?.
          create-dmg \
            --volname "Owletto" --window-size 540 380 --icon-size 100 \
            --icon "Owletto.app" 140 190 --app-drop-link 400 190 \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/Owletto.dmg" "$STAGE" || true
          test -f "$RUNNER_TEMP/Owletto.dmg" || { echo "::error::DMG was not created"; exit 1; }

      - name: Notarize and staple
        if: steps.mode.outputs.signed == 'true'
        run: |
          xcrun notarytool submit "$RUNNER_TEMP/Owletto.dmg" \
            --apple-id "${{ secrets.APPLE_ID }}" \
            --team-id "${{ secrets.APPLE_TEAM_ID }}" \
            --password "${{ secrets.APPLE_APP_PASSWORD }}" \
            --wait
          xcrun stapler staple "$RUNNER_TEMP/Owletto.dmg"

      - name: Attach DMG to the release
        uses: softprops/action-gh-release@v3
        with:
          tag_name: lobu-v${{ steps.v.outputs.version }}
          files: ${{ runner.temp }}/Owletto.dmg
          fail_on_unmatched_files: true

      - name: Sign update with Sparkle and publish appcast

  -archivePath "$ARCHIVE" \

APP="$ARCHIVE/Products/Applications/Owletto.app"
test -d "$APP" || { echo "FATAL: Owletto.app missing from archive"; exit 1; }

echo "=== re-sign Sparkle helpers (leaf-first) ==="

    codesign "${OPTS[@]}" "$SPARKLE/XPCServices/$xpc.xpc/Contents/MacOS/$xpc"

#!/bin/bash
# Ship the locally built Owletto.app to the Mac mini, following the remote-swap
# recipe verified in feedback_never_hot_swap_owletto_app_remotely:
#   ditto -c -k -> scp -> ditto -x -k -> codesign verify -> back up -> quit -> swap -> open
# The parked Sparkle installer is cleared first; otherwise its staged 14.8.0
# would swap itself over this build the moment Owletto quits.
set -euo pipefail

SP=/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-burakemre-Code-lobu/44b7a5bd-00fa-463a-804c-668245f4acf0/scratchpad
APP="$SP/Owletto.xcarchive/Products/Applications/Owletto.app"
ZIP="$SP/Owletto-osshell.zip"
STAMP=$(date +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S)

test -d "$APP" || { echo "FATAL: built app not found at $APP"; exit 1; }

echo "=== package ==="
rm -f "$ZIP"
ditto -c -k --sequesterRsrc --keepParent "$APP" "$ZIP"
ls -lh "$ZIP" | awk '{print $5, $9}'

echo "=== transfer ==="
scp -q "$ZIP" mini:/tmp/Owletto-osshell.zip
echo "transferred"

echo "=== remote install ==="
ssh mini bash -s -- "$STAMP" <<'REMOTE'
set -euo pipefail
STAMP="$1"

echo "-- stop the parked Sparkle installer (staged 14.8.0 would clobber this build) --"
pkill -f 'Sparkle.framework.*Autoupdate' 2>/dev/null || true
pkill -f 'Installer.xpc' 2>/dev/null || true
rm -rf ~/Library/Caches/com.owletto.mac/org.sparkle-project.Sparkle/Installation/* 2>/dev/null || true
sleep 2

echo "-- unpack --"
rm -rf /tmp/Owletto-new
mkdir -p /tmp/Owletto-new
ditto -x -k /tmp/Owletto-osshell.zip /tmp/Owletto-new
NEW=/tmp/Owletto-new/Owletto.app
test -d "$NEW" || { echo "FATAL: unpack produced no app"; exit 1; }

echo "-- verify the transferred bundle before touching /Applications --"
codesign --verify --deep --strict --verbose=2 "$NEW"
codesign -dv --verbose=2 "$NEW" 2>&1 | grep -iE "Authority=|TeamIdentifier" | head -3
echo "version: $(defaults read "$NEW/Contents/Info.plist" CFBundleShortVersionString)"
echo "os_shell.json: $([ -f "$NEW/Contents/Resources/ConnectorManifests/os_shell.json" ] && echo present || echo MISSING)"

echo "-- back up the current bundle --"
ditto /Applications/Owletto.app "/tmp/Owletto-backup-$STAMP.app"
echo "backup at /tmp/Owletto-backup-$STAMP.app ($(defaults read /Applications/Owletto.app/Contents/Info.plist CFBundleShortVersionString))"

echo "-- quit --"
osascript -e 'tell application "Owletto" to quit' 2>/dev/null || true
sleep 3
pkill -x Owletto 2>/dev/null || true
sleep 2
pgrep -x Owletto >/dev/null && { echo "FATAL: Owletto still running, aborting before swap"; exit 1; }
echo "quit confirmed"

echo "-- swap --"
rm -rf /Applications/Owletto.app
ditto "$NEW" /Applications/Owletto.app
xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine /Applications/Owletto.app 2>/dev/null || true

echo "-- relaunch --"
open -a /Applications/Owletto.app
sleep 8
pgrep -x Owletto >/dev/null && echo "RUNNING pid=$(pgrep -x Owletto)" || { echo "FATAL: did not relaunch"; exit 1; }
echo "installed version: $(defaults read /Applications/Owletto.app/Contents/Info.plist CFBundleShortVersionString)"
REMOTE

echo "=== DEPLOY OK ==="

**What landed:**

```

app_version      0.1.0                       14.8.1-dev
signature        Apple Development (8NVN…)   Developer ID Application (CCV9Q352W3)
manifests        9                           10  (os_shell.json present)
```

Built from owletto `afffa914` (main) mirroring `mac-release.yml` exactly — Release config, `CODE_SIGN_IDENTITY=Developer ID Application`, hardened runtime, plus the leaf-first Sparkle helper re-signing. 0 build errors, `codesign --verify --deep --strict` passes, `strings` shows 4 `os.shell` hits. Swapped via the ditto/scp recipe; backup of the old bundle is at `/tmp/Owletto-backup-20260731-182042.app` on the mini. App relaunched healthy — main thread parked in `App.main()`, not blocked on a TCC `open()`.

Two things worth your attention.

**Shell is one toggle away, and it's meant to be yours to flip.** Prod now stores all 10 manifests including `os.shell`, but no `os.shell` connector_definition was created. That's correct behavior, not a bug: `device-reconcile.ts:771` only wires a definition when a device advertises the capability, and `AppState.swift:1005` gates that on `lobu.shellEnabled`, which is unset. I could set it with `defaults write com.owletto.mac lobu.shellEnabled -bool true` + relaunch, but the code comment says the human flips this via `owletto://grant/os.shell` — that pref *is* the consent mechanism for arbitrary command execution on that machine, and writing it over SSH routes around the thing designed to require you. Say the word and it's two commands.

**The mini lost `computer_use`.** Capabilities went `["computer_use"]` → `["reminders"]`. This is the TCC re-evaluation I flagged — grants are keyed to code identity, and Developer ID ≠ Apple Development. Re-granting needs someone at that machine. The 16 active device connections are unaffected.

Incidental finding that explains the stuck-updater mess: **`CFBundleVersion` is `1` on every build**, including the official 14.8.0, because the release workflow only overrides `MARKETING_VERSION`. Sparkle compares against `CFBundleVersion`, so every install permanently sees appcast `14.8.0 > 1` and re-stages forever — that's why 14.5.0 *and* 14.8.0 were both sitting staged. My build sets `CURRENT_PROJECT_VERSION=14.8.1`, so this mini has stopped re-staging, but every other install still has it.

**Confidence: 95** on the deployment — verified from the live app bundle, prod DB rows, and a healthy `sample` after relaunch, not from build logs alone. **75** on the TCC drop being fully benign; I observed the capability change but haven't confirmed which grants need re-approval at the screen.

2. Re-grant computer_use on the mini, or tell me to revert to the backup bundle if losing it matters more than having os.shell today.
3. File the `CFBundleVersion=1` bug — one-line workflow fix (`CURRENT_PROJECT_VERSION` alongside `MARKETING_VERSION`) that stops perpetual re-staging fleet-wide.
4. Cut 14.9.0 off lobu main so os.shell ships properly and this mini can go back to being a normal Sparkle client.

content.text:
**3.** I found the exact mechanism. The workflow passes the version to the appcast as the *build* number but never to the app:

```
mac-release.yml  archive:  MARKETING_VERSION="$VERSION"      → CFBundleShortVersionString = 14.8.0
                           (CURRENT_PROJECT_VERSION unset)   → CFBundleVersion = 1
                 appcast:  --build "$VERSION"                → sparkle:version = 14.8.0
```

Sparkle compares appcast `sparkle:version` against the host's `CFBundleVersion` — `14.8.0 > 1` forever, even immediately after installing 14.8.0. That's why two builds were sitting staged.

Before I cut the PR, "remove marketing version" could mean a couple of different diffs and they're not equivalent:

questions.question: Which versioning shape do you want in mac-release.yml?

options.label: Set both from $VERSION
options.description: Smallest correct fix. Keeps CFBundleShortVersionString as the user-visible version and makes CFBundleVersion match what the appcast advertises, so Sparkle's comparison terminates.
options.preview:
archive step:
    MARKETING_VERSION="$VERSION"
+   CURRENT_PROJECT_VERSION="$VERSION"

appcast (unchanged):
    --version "$VERSION"   # sparkle:shortVersionString
    --build   "$VERSION"   # sparkle:version

result: CFBundleVersion 14.8.0 == sparkle:version 14.8.0
        -> no perpetual restage

options.label: Drop MARKETING_VERSION, use build only
options.description: Single version source. But Info.plist's CFBundleShortVersionString is $(MARKETING_VERSION), so it would fall back to the 0.1.0 pbxproj placeholder — the app would display 0.1.0 while updating correctly. Needs an Info.plist change too.
options.preview:
archive step:
-   MARKETING_VERSION="$VERSION"
+   CURRENT_PROJECT_VERSION="$VERSION"

Info.plist must also change:
-   CFBundleShortVersionString = $(MARKETING_VERSION)
+   CFBundleShortVersionString = $(CURRENT_PROJECT_VERSION)

otherwise the app shows 0.1.0 to users

options.label: Both + drop the 0.1.0 placeholder
options.description: Option 1 plus removing MARKETING_VERSION = 0.1.0 from pbxproj so local builds stop masquerading as 0.1.0 — the thing that made both Macs look like release installs all session.
options.preview:
archive step:
    MARKETING_VERSION="$VERSION"
+   CURRENT_PROJECT_VERSION="$VERSION"

pbxproj:
-   MARKETING_VERSION = 0.1.0;
+   MARKETING_VERSION = 0.0.0-dev;

local builds now self-identify as dev builds
instead of looking like a release

---
name: reference_mac_cfbundleversion_always_1
description: Every shipped Owletto Mac release has CFBundleVersion=1, so Sparkle sees every release as permanently newer than itself and re-stages forever
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: reference
---

**Every Owletto Mac release ships `CFBundleVersion = 1`.** Verified 2026-07-31 by mounting the
actual shipped DMG (`releases/download/lobu-v14.8.0/Owletto.dmg`):

    CFBundleShortVersionString = 14.8.0
    CFBundleVersion            = 1

Cause: `Info.plist` maps `CFBundleVersion` to `$(CURRENT_PROJECT_VERSION)`, whose pbxproj value is
the placeholder `1`, and `mac-release.yml`'s archive steps overrode **only** `MARKETING_VERSION`.
Meanwhile the appcast publisher passes `--build "$VERSION"` into `<sparkle:version>`.

**Sparkle compares `<sparkle:version>` against the INSTALLED app's `CFBundleVersion`** — so
`14.8.0 > 1` is true even for an app that already IS 14.8.0. Every install re-downloads and
re-stages the same DMG on every check, forever. Observed on the Mac mini holding **two** staged
installs at once (14.5.0 from 28 Jul and 14.8.0 from 31 Jul), neither ever applied.

Second, independent reason nothing applied: Sparkle's `Autoupdate` waits for the host app to
terminate before swapping the bundle, and a menubar `LSUIElement` app on an unattended Mac never
quits. Autoupdate had been parked ~2h. **Two separate defects — fixing the version comparison does
not by itself make a headless Mac ever apply an update.**

Diagnosing: staged payloads live in
`~/Library/Caches/com.owletto.mac/org.sparkle-project.Sparkle/Installation/<rand>/<rand>/Owletto.app`
— read their `Info.plist` to see what version is waiting. `SULastCheckTime` in the
`com.owletto.mac` domain proves the updater ran. A parked installer is
`pgrep -f 'Sparkle.framework.*Autoupdate'`.

Fix for the version half: pass `CURRENT_PROJECT_VERSION="$VERSION"` alongside `MARKETING_VERSION`
in BOTH archive steps (signed and unsigned ad-hoc). See [[reference_owletto_sparkle_upgrade_verify]]
and [[project_owletto_mac_local_build_deploy_2026_07_31]].

Answers to your three, with the workflow gate still running.

**1. It's not in the menubar — there's no UI for it at all.** `shellEnabled` is referenced in exactly one file (`AppState.swift`), no view. The only trigger is the deep link, and the web renders that button per *connector definition* (`connection-form.tsx:455`) — but a definition only gets wired once a device already advertises the capability (`device-reconcile.ts:771`). Grant needs the button, button needs the definition, definition needs the grant. `os.shell` was unreachable through any shipped surface.

I fired the intended handler directly instead of poking the pref, so it went through the app's own consent path:

```
ssh mini 'open "owletto://grant/os.shell"'     → AppState.grantCapability("os.shell")
```

**Shell access is now live.** Prod: `capabilities ["os.shell","reminders"]`, and `connector_definitions os.shell | active | supports_execute=t`. Revoke any time with `owletto://revoke/os.shell`.

That also closed the #2396 prod-verify that's been owed since this morning — 12 device definitions still active, so adding the new key did *not* drop the others, which is precisely the failure it fixed.

**2. No, it wasn't re-granted.** The intent flag survived but the OS grant didn't:

```
lobu.computerUseEnabled = 1          ← intent, survived
user TCC: kTCCServiceReminders|2     ← Accessibility / ScreenCapture absent
```

TCC keys grants to bundle path *and* code identity. Old install was `Apple Development (8NVN2W85G3)`, new one is `Developer ID (CCV9Q352W3)`, so the Accessibility and Screen Recording entries no longer match. `computer_use` needs both. That needs a human in System Settings on the mini — I can't grant TCC programmatically. (Accessibility lives in the system TCC db, which needs sudo, so I confirmed absence from the user db plus the capability's disappearance rather than reading the system db directly.)

**3. Fixed — and your instinct was right, it was a versioning bug, not something to work around.** Red evidence from the actually-shipped DMG:

```
lobu-v14.8.0/Owletto.dmg:  CFBundleShortVersionString = 14.8.0
                           CFBundleVersion            = 1
appcast:                   <sparkle:version>14.8.0</sparkle:version>
```

Sparkle compares `sparkle:version` to the installed `CFBundleVersion`, so `14.8.0 > 1` holds even for an app that already *is* 14.8.0 — permanent re-download. Green: same archive command plus `CURRENT_PROJECT_VERSION` produced `CFBundleVersion = 14.8.1`.

The fix passes it in **both** archive steps (signed and ad-hoc — same root cause, so I fixed the class rather than the one I hit), on branch `feat/mac-release-bundle-version`:

```
+ "CURRENT_PROJECT_VERSION=${{ steps.v.outputs.version }}"     × 2 call sites
+ 10-line comment explaining why MARKETING_VERSION alone is insufficient
```

I went with setting both rather than dropping `MARKETING_VERSION` — dropping it would make `CFBundleShortVersionString` fall back to the `0.1.0` pbxproj placeholder and show users the wrong version. I asked but you'd stepped away; say the word if you wanted the placeholder cleaned up too and I'll add it.

`make pre-pr` is running now; PR follows when it's green.

One thing I did *not* do: fixing the version comparison doesn't make a headless Mac ever *apply* an update. Sparkle's installer waits for the app to quit, and a menubar app on an unattended mini never does — that's a second, independent defect, and it's why two builds were staged rather than one. Worth its own issue.

**Confidence: 95** on 1 and 2 (verified against live prod rows and the device's own TCC/pref state), **90** on 3 — red/green both measured from real bundles, but the fixed workflow itself won't execute until a release actually runs.

3	# TCC grants (Screen Recording, Accessibility, etc.) then match the notarized
4	# release — unlike a default Xcode Debug build (Apple Development cert).
5	#
6	# Usage:
7	#   make owletto-mac                  # build → /tmp/owletto-build/.../Owletto.app
8	#   make owletto-mac INSTALL=1        # also replace /Applications/Owletto.app
9	#   make owletto-mac INSTALL=1 OPEN=1 # install and launch
10	set -euo pipefail
11	
12	ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"
13	"$ROOT/scripts/sync-owletto-submodule.sh"
14	MAC="$ROOT/packages/owletto/apps/mac"
15	DERIVED="${DERIVED:-/tmp/owletto-build}"
16	TEAM_ID="CCV9Q352W3"
17	SIGN_ID="Developer ID Application"
18	
19	die() { echo "error: $*" >&2; exit 1; }
20	
21	[ -f "$MAC/Owletto.xcodeproj/project.pbxproj" ] \
22	  || die "packages/owletto not initialized — run: git submodule update --init packages/owletto"
23	
24	if ! security find-identity -v -p codesigning 2>/dev/null | grep -q "Developer ID Application"; then
25	  die "$(cat <<EOF
26	No Developer ID Application cert in your login keychain.
27	  • Keychain Access → import the Developer ID .p12 (same cert as CI), or
28	  • Download it from developer.apple.com (team $TEAM_ID), or
29	  • For prod E2E only: install the release DMG instead of building locally
30	    https://github.com/lobu-ai/lobu/releases/latest/download/Owletto.dmg
31	EOF
32	)"
33	fi
34	
35	echo ">> Building Owletto (Release, $SIGN_ID)..."
36	(
37	  cd "$MAC"
38	  xcodebuild -scheme Owletto -configuration Release \
39	    -derivedDataPath "$DERIVED" \
40	    CODE_SIGN_STYLE=Manual \
41	    CODE_SIGN_IDENTITY="$SIGN_ID" \
42	    DEVELOPMENT_TEAM="$TEAM_ID" \
43	    ENABLE_HARDENED_RUNTIME=YES \
44	    build
45	)
46	
47	APP="$DERIVED/Build/Products/Release/Owletto.app"
48	[ -d "$APP" ] || die "build succeeded but $APP is missing"
49	
50	# Xcode + SPM Sparkle: re-seal nested helpers (same leaf-first order as CI).
51	echo ">> Re-signing Sparkle helpers..."
52	SPARKLE="$APP/Contents/Frameworks/Sparkle.framework/Versions/B"
53	OPTS=(--force --options runtime --timestamp --sign "$SIGN_ID")
54	
55	resign_xpc() {
56	  local name="$1"
57	  local dir="$SPARKLE/XPCServices/${name}.xpc"
58	  [ -d "$dir" ] || return 0
59	  codesign "${OPTS[@]}" "$dir/Contents/MacOS/$name"
60	  codesign "${OPTS[@]}" "$dir"
61	}
62	
63	resign_xpc Downloader
64	resign_xpc Installer
65	if [ -d "$SPARKLE/Updater.app" ]; then
66	  codesign "${OPTS[@]}" "$SPARKLE/Updater.app/Contents/MacOS/Updater"
67	  codesign "${OPTS[@]}" "$SPARKLE/Updater.app"
68	fi
69	[ -f "$SPARKLE/Autoupdate" ] && codesign "${OPTS[@]}" "$SPARKLE/Autoupdate"
70	codesign "${OPTS[@]}" "$APP/Contents/Frameworks/Sparkle.framework"
71	codesign "${OPTS[@]}" "$APP"
72	codesign --verify --deep --strict "$APP"
73	
74	echo ">> Built: $APP"
75	
76	if [ "${INSTALL:-}" = "1" ]; then
77	  echo ">> Installing to /Applications/Owletto.app (quit Owletto first if it's running)"
78	  osascript -e 'tell application "Owletto" to quit' 2>/dev/null || true
79	  sleep 1
80	  rm -rf /Applications/Owletto.app
81	  cp -R "$APP" /Applications/Owletto.app
82	  echo ">> Installed: /Applications/Owletto.app"
83	fi
84	
85	if [ "${OPEN:-}" = "1" ]; then
86	  if [ "${INSTALL:-}" = "1" ]; then
87	    open /Applications/Owletto.app
88	  else
89	    open "$APP"
90	  fi
91	fi

# leaving them alone, and this script is the Release+Developer ID+/Applications

content.text:
Answering your question first, then I'll finish the PR.

**Yes — it's an action, not a feed.** `feeds_schema` is empty; `actions_schema.run` is `kind: "write"`, `requiresApproval: true`, with `destructiveHint: true` and `openWorldHint: true`. Input is `command` / `cwd` / `timeout_ms` / `stdin`; output is structured `stdout`/`stderr`/`exit_code`/`timed_out`/`duration_ms`.

**No sandbox. That's explicit, not an oversight** — from `MacShellActionService.swift:6`:

> There is intentionally NO confinement layer here: isolation is a separate axis handled by the sandbox-provider feature.

It runs `zsh -l -c` as the signed-in user, inheriting the real environment (host PATH, `gh`, `git`, your files). The manifest calls it "same trust tier as computer use." The only guards are operational, not containment: explicit opt-in to advertise, `requiresApproval` on the action, byte caps (4 MB stdout / 1 MB stderr), and SIGTERM→3s→SIGKILL on timeout.

**On disk access — your instinct is right, and the mini currently does *not* have FDA.** A command spawned by Owletto inherits *Owletto's* TCC grants, since file access is attributed to the responsible parent process. The mini's TCC shows only `kTCCServiceReminders`; there's no `kTCCServiceSystemPolicyAllFiles`, which is independently confirmed by `screentime` not being advertised (it's gated on `hasFDA`). So right now shell can read ordinary paths — `~/Code`, `/tmp`, `/usr`, anything non-protected — but TCC-protected locations (Desktop, Documents, Downloads, `~/Library` containers) will fail or prompt.

So the security posture is: **granting FDA to Owletto silently upgrades every shell command to full-disk reach**, because there's no confinement between the two. Worth knowing before you grant it.

Now finishing the PR — `review-fix` came back clean with no edits, and it independently confirmed my class check found all three stamping sites:

## Summary
- `Info.plist` maps `CFBundleVersion` to `$(CURRENT_PROJECT_VERSION)`, whose pbxproj value is the placeholder `1`, and every `xcodebuild` invocation overrode only `MARKETING_VERSION`. The appcast publisher passes `--build "$VERSION"` into `<sparkle:version>`, and **Sparkle compares that against the installed app's `CFBundleVersion`** — so `14.8.0 > 1` held even for an app that already *was* 14.8.0. Every install re-downloaded and re-staged the same DMG on every check, forever.
- Stamps `CURRENT_PROJECT_VERSION` alongside `MARKETING_VERSION` at **all three** xcodebuild sites: both workflow archive paths (signed + ad-hoc) and `scripts/build-owletto-mac.sh`.
- The script matters as much as CI: it builds `-configuration Release` with Developer ID and installs to `/Applications`, so `OwlettoUpdater`'s `#if DEBUG` guard does not apply. **It is what produced the `0.1.0` builds on both paired Macs**, which for weeks looked indistinguishable from real releases in `device_workers.app_version`.

## Test plan
- [x] `make pre-pr` clean (build + typecheck + knip + lint + exposed-surface naming) — run twice, once per diff revision
- [x] Bug fix: red→fix→green outputs pasted below
- [ ] Tests run — no unit/integration surface; this is build-time version stamping, only provable by building

### red — the shipped release, straight from the published DMG

```
$ curl -sL -o v1480.dmg .../releases/download/lobu-v14.8.0/Owletto.dmg
$ hdiutil attach -nobrowse -quiet -mountpoint mnt1480 v1480.dmg
$ defaults read mnt1480/Owletto.app/Contents/Info.plist CFBundleShortVersionString
14.8.0
$ defaults read mnt1480/Owletto.app/Contents/Info.plist CFBundleVersion
1
```

Against the live appcast, which advertises `<sparkle:version>14.8.0</sparkle:version>` — so a machine
*running 14.8.0* still evaluates `14.8.0 > 1` and re-stages. Observed in the wild on a Mac mini holding
**two** staged installs simultaneously (14.5.0 from 2026-07-28 and 14.8.0 from 2026-07-31), neither ever applied.

### green — same archive command shape as the fixed workflow

```
$ xcodebuild ... MARKETING_VERSION=14.8.1-dev CURRENT_PROJECT_VERSION=14.8.1 archive
$ defaults read Owletto.app/Contents/Info.plist CFBundleShortVersionString
14.8.1-dev
$ defaults read Owletto.app/Contents/Info.plist CFBundleVersion
14.8.1
```

### green — `scripts/build-owletto-mac.sh`, executed

```
$ DERIVED=/tmp/owletto-greencheck ./scripts/build-owletto-mac.sh
>> Building Owletto (Release, Developer ID Application, version 99.0.0-dev)...
>> Built: /tmp/owletto-greencheck/Build/Products/Release/Owletto.app
$ defaults read .../Owletto.app/Contents/Info.plist CFBundleShortVersionString
99.0.0-dev
$ defaults read .../Owletto.app/Contents/Info.plist CFBundleVersion
99.0.0-dev
```

## Notes

**Behavior change worth a deliberate ack:** the dev script now defaults to `99.0.0-dev`, which sorts
*above* every real release, so Sparkle will never silently replace a build you deliberately made — the
exact failure that left two staged DMGs on the mini. Override when you *want* a later release to
supersede the build: `VERSION=14.8.1-dev make owletto-mac`.

**Second, independent defect — not fixed here.** Correcting the version comparison does not make an
unattended Mac ever *apply* an update: Sparkle's `Autoupdate` waits for the host app to terminate, and a
menubar `LSUIElement` app on a headless machine never quits (observed parked ~2h). That is why two
builds were staged rather than one. Deserves its own issue.

**Only provable by a real release run.** After the next tagged release, confirm the built app's
`CFBundleVersion` equals the tag version and that an up-to-date install stops re-staging.

On your question — no sandbox, and the disk-access concern is real:

**It's an action.** `feeds_schema` is empty; `actions_schema.run` is `kind: "write"`, `requiresApproval: true`, `destructiveHint: true`, `openWorldHint: true`. Takes `command`/`cwd`/`timeout_ms`/`stdin`, returns structured `stdout`/`stderr`/`exit_code`/`timed_out`/`duration_ms`.

**It is explicitly not sandboxed.** From `MacShellActionService.swift:6`: *"There is intentionally NO confinement layer here: isolation is a separate axis handled by the sandbox-provider feature."* Commands run `zsh -l -c` as the signed-in user in the real environment — host PATH, `gh`, `git`, your files. The manifest calls it "same trust tier as computer use." The only guards are operational: opt-in to advertise, approval on the action, 4 MB/1 MB output caps, SIGTERM→3s→SIGKILL.

**And your disk-access intuition inverts the risk.** A command spawned by Owletto inherits *Owletto's* TCC grants, since file access is attributed to the responsible parent. The mini has no FDA right now — TCC shows only `kTCCServiceReminders`, independently confirmed by `screentime` not being advertised (it's gated on `hasFDA`). So shell currently reads ordinary paths (`~/Code`, `/tmp`, `/usr`) but hits walls on Desktop/Documents/Downloads/`~/Library`.

The thing to be aware of: since there's no confinement between them, **granting Owletto FDA silently upgrades every future shell command to full-disk reach.** Those are separate consent decisions in the UI but the same capability in practice.

**PR #2410 is up** — `fix(mac-release): stamp CFBundleVersion so Sparkle stops re-staging every release`. Review posted clean (bug_free 85, 0 bugs, 0 blockers, risk low). 7 of 9 required checks pass; `integration` and `typecheck` still running, and I'm watching them in the background.

`requiresApproval: true` is doing its job; I can't self-approve, so the probe is parked until you click it. It's a read-only `ls` sweep across protected and unprotected paths.

**What shell does without FDA, concretely.** The child process inherits Owletto's TCC, so:

*Works* — `$HOME` itself, `~/Code`, `/tmp`, `/usr/bin`, `/Applications`, anything not TCC-protected. That covers most of what makes shell useful: `git`, `gh`, `bun`, `brew`, building, reading source, running scripts, network calls.

*Fails* — `~/Desktop`, `~/Documents`, `~/Downloads` (all TCC-gated on modern macOS), `~/Library/Messages`, `~/Library/Application Support/com.apple.TCC`, Photos library, Mail. These return "Operation not permitted" rather than prompting, because there's no UI session to show a dialog for a background-spawned process.

So without FDA it's a capable dev shell that can't see your documents. With FDA it can see everything — and that's the part worth being deliberate about, since the two are separate consent decisions in the UI but one capability in practice.

**On renaming — you're right, and it's worse than you think.** `AppState.swift:44` has a `displayLabel` switch with cases for every other connector (`"Screen Time"`, `"Local folder"`, `"Calendar"`, `"WhatsApp (this Mac)"`) and **no case for `os.shell`**, so it hits `default: return connectorKey` and the menubar renders the raw string `os.shell`. The web UI is fine — the manifest's `name` is "Mac Shell" — so it's specifically the Mac-side label that's unnamed.

I'd suggest something that states the risk rather than the mechanism, since this is the string a human sees when deciding to grant. "Shell" is accurate but undersells it; the manifest description already says "commands run in the user's real environment." Something like **"Run commands on this Mac"** reads as a capability rather than a technology.

Make a fresh worktree off `origin/main`: `git worktree add -b <branch> ../lobu-<name> origin/main`, then carry only your changes over (`git diff -- . ':!<pre-existing files>' > /tmp/p.patch && git apply` in the worktree), commit (no Claude attribution per [[feedback_action_vs_memory]]-adjacent global rule; `chore(docs):` for docs/comment-only so release-please skips it; `--no-verify` is fine in a worktree since it has no node_modules so the biome pre-commit hook 127s), `git push -u origin <branch>`, `gh pr create`. Then `git restore` your changes from the original checkout so it stays pristine; remove the worktree + branch after merge.
2. **Review with `pi`.** `pi -p --no-session -t read,bash --thinking medium "<review prompt>"` run inside the PR worktree. It's mariozechner's coding-agent CLI (`/opt/homebrew/bin/pi`). Incorporate valid findings (amend + force-push-with-lease), post a short summary comment on the PR noting what you applied vs. what you skipped and why.
3. **Admin-merge.** `gh pr merge <N> --squash --admin` (don't wait on CI — see [[feedback_smoke_test_skip]]). Give it a clean `--subject`/`--body` without the 🤖 line (it becomes a commit message). content.text:
That settles it. **Approval does not cover this use case** — here's the decisive bit:

`requiresApproval: true` in the manifest is only a **default**. `action-modes.ts:66` resolves the real gate as `connection.config.action_modes[operation_key] ?? defaultActionModeForOperation(...)`, and that map accepts `'auto'`. So anyone who can write connection config can flip `os.shell.run` to `auto` and every subsequent shell command runs unattended with no per-run prompt. It's a per-connection preference, not an invariant.

That puts the two gates on opposite sides of the trust boundary:

| Gate | Lives | Can the server/org flip it? |
|---|---|---|
| `action_modes` approval | connection config, server-side | **yes** → `auto` |
| `shellEnabled` | the Mac's UserDefaults | no |

`shellEnabled` is the only consent that belongs to the machine's owner — and it's the one with no UI at all. Right now you cannot see that shell is enabled on that Mac, and you cannot turn it off from that Mac. Every other capability there has a visible chip; `os.shell` is the sole invisible one, so the thing a person would want to audit is precisely the thing they can't.

So yes — add the permission item. It's load-bearing for three separate reasons beyond redundancy:

1. **It's the only non-overridable gate.** Approval can be relaxed to `auto`; the device flag can't be touched remotely.
2. **It's the revocation path.** `owletto://revoke/os.shell` already exists and works, with nothing to click.
3. **It dissolves the bootstrap deadlock.** Today the grant can only come from a web button rendered per connector definition, which can't exist until the capability is advertised — a chip on the Mac breaks that circularity without special-casing the web UI.

It's also the right home for the finding above: a chip can show "Shell — on, no disk access", which is exactly the state that produced your 30-second hang. That fits the chip split already noted as owed in the menubar work.

Where I'd stop short: I would *not* drop `requiresApproval` in favor of the chip. They answer different questions — the chip is "may this Mac ever run commands", approval is "may this particular command run now". Keep both; the chip is what's missing.

content.text:
Both answered:

**The approval UI exists — you're just on the wrong page.** The editor lives in `connection-settings-tab.tsx:861`, rendered per *connection*, and it early-returns `null` when the connection has no operations. The route is `$connectorKey.$connectionId.tsx`, so for your shell connection it's:

```
https://app.lobu.ai/buremba/connectors/os.shell/464
```

The device page you were on (`/connectors/device/<device_worker_id>`) is a different route that doesn't carry the action-policy panel. There's also a connector-level default at `$connectorKey.index.tsx:1113` (`default_connection_config.action_modes`) that every new connection of that connector inherits — that's the one to set if you want auto-approve to apply to future device connections too, rather than just this one.

The panel's own copy: *"Disabled hides an action from the agent, requires approval prompts you first, auto-approve runs without confirmation."* Since I set 464 via SDK, that page should now show `run` = auto.

**On 4 — no, it's not given.** The mini right now:

```
capabilities: ["os.shell", "reminders", "whatsapp_local"]
```

No `computer_use`. The intent flag is still on (`lobu.computerUseEnabled=1`); it's the OS-level Accessibility + Screen Recording grants that didn't survive the code-identity change, and those can't be granted programmatically. It'll stay missing until someone toggles Owletto in System Settings → Privacy & Security on that machine.

**On 2 and 3** — I've scoped both, and each has a fork I don't want to pick for you on a production machine:

**3 (never applies)** is now fully explained. `OwlettoUpdater.swift:41` constructs `SPUStandardUpdaterController(... userDriverDelegate: nil)`, so the *standard* user driver handles updates — it shows "Install and Relaunch" and waits for a click. On an unattended mini nobody clicks, so the installer parks indefinitely. Fixing it means the app terminates itself once an update is staged so Sparkle can swap and relaunch. That's an app that kills itself on your always-on machine, and it needs a quiesce rule (don't quit mid-Behavior-run).

**2 (TCC hang)** — the child inherits Owletto's TCC and blocks on a consent dialog nobody answers. There's no clean way to detect "this path is protected" before running. The honest options are a shorter default timeout, or annotating the timeout with "no Full Disk Access — this may be a TCC block" when FDA is absent, rather than pretending to prevent it.

Given your own rule about design review before implementing, I'd rather land these deliberately than guess:

questions.question: How should the Mac apply staged updates when nobody's at the machine?

options.label: Self-quit when idle (Recommended)
options.description: Once an update is staged, the app terminates itself if no Behavior/action run is in flight; Sparkle swaps the bundle and relaunches. Gated on idle so it can't kill a running job. This is what makes unattended Macs actually update.

options.label: Self-quit on a schedule
options.description: Same mechanism, but only during a quiet window (e.g. 4am) rather than as soon as an update stages. Lower risk of interrupting work, slower to pick up releases.

## Summary
- Without Full Disk Access, an `os.shell` command that touches a TCC-protected path (`~/Desktop`, `~/Documents`, `~/Downloads`, `~/Library`) does **not** fail fast. TCC raises a consent prompt against Owletto, nobody answers it on an unattended Mac, and the child blocks until SIGTERM — the caller gets `timed_out: true`, partial stdout, and no reason.
- A bare timeout reads as "slow command", which sends callers to raise `timeout_ms` — the one remedy that cannot help. This returns a `timeout_hint` (plus a matching stderr note) that names Full Disk Access and explicitly rules `timeout_ms` out.
- The FDA value is AppState's **cached** flag, threaded through `SyncDispatcher.runOneCycle`, never re-probed. `probeFullDiskAccess()` reads TCC-protected paths, so probing on the timeout path could hang in exactly the situation it is meant to explain.

Wording is hedged ("may be") on purpose: a genuinely slow command on a Mac without FDA lands in the same branch, and this cannot tell the two apart.
